docs.title: Configurator
docs.text:
Configurator is a CLI that generates an application-hub compatible YAML configuration from a set of Python-defined profiles.

It is designed to:

  • keep profiles versioned in Git
  • support multiple profiles in one output file
  • allow operator overrides via CLI options (CPU/memory/image/groups/node selectors)
  • support profile plugins loaded from external folders
  • preserve multi-line values using YAML literal blocks (|) for readability
  • support structured manifests (YAML objects), not string blobs

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
Generate a config enabling multiple profiles:

dump-config \
  --profiles coder_app,gpu_coder_app,remote_desktop,qgis_remote_desktop,coder_dask_gateway_app,jupyterlab_small \
  --groups group-a,group-b,group-c \
  --output config.yaml

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
A profile is a Python class registered into the ProfileRegistry with a unique slug.

Profiles define defaults for:

  • container image
  • CPU/memory limits/guarantees
  • volumes
  • config maps
  • init containers
  • manifests
  • role bindings
  • node selector
  • env vars

docs.title: Overrides
docs.text:
Operators can override profile defaults without changing code, e.g.:

dump-config \
  --profiles coder_app \
  --groups group-a \
  --override coder_app:cpu_limit=4 \
  --override coder_app:mem_limit=8G

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Start here: Getting started

Role-based onboarding: Onboarding

For users/operators: CLI docs

For developers: Developer guide

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
This guide explains how to install and run the dump-config CLI.

For role-specific paths, see Onboarding. For an EOEPCA multi-application example, see EOEPCA extra config tutorial.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
From the project root:

hatch env create
hatch run dump-config --help

Or install editable:

pip install -e .
dump-config --help

docs.title: Generate a configuration
docs.text:
dump-config \
  --profiles coder_app,gpu_coder_app \
  --groups group-a,group-b \
  --output config.yaml

docs.title: Validate output
docs.text:
Inspect the generated YAML:

yq '.profiles[].definition.slug' config.yaml

docs.title: List available profiles
docs.text: dump-config --list-profiles

docs.title: Inspect a profile
docs.text: dump-config --describe-profile coder_app

docs.title: Common environment variables
docs.text:
All CLI options support envvars:

  • ENABLED_PROFILES
  • GROUPS
  • OUTPUT_FILE
  • STORAGE_CLASS_RWO
  • STORAGE_CLASS_RWX

Example:

export ENABLED_PROFILES="coder_app,gpu_coder_app"
export GROUPS="group-a,group-b"
dump-config

docs.title: Basic generation
docs.text:
dump-config \
  --profiles coder_app,remote_desktop \
  --groups group-a,group-b \
  --output config.yaml

docs.title: Storage classes
docs.text:
Override storage class values:

dump-config \
  --profiles coder_app \
  --groups group-a \
  --storage-class-rwo standard \
  --storage-class-rwx standard-rwx \
  --output config.yaml

docs.title: Large profile set
docs.text:
dump-config \
  --profiles coder_app,gpu_coder_app,remote_desktop,qgis_remote_desktop,panoply_remote_desktop,snap_remote_desktop,coder_dask_gateway_app,jupyterlab_small \
  --groups group-a,group-b,group-c \
  --output config.yaml

docs.title: YAML formatting
docs.text:
Configurator preserves multi-line values (scripts/configs) using literal blocks:

content: |
  echo "Initializing environment..."
  export HOME=/workspace

This improves readability and prevents YAML escaping issues.

docs.title: List all registered profiles
docs.text: dump-config --list-profiles

docs.title: Describe a profile
docs.text:
dump-config --describe-profile coder_dask_gateway_app

This prints:

  • display name
  • description
  • image
  • CPU/memory defaults
  • volumes
  • env vars
  • manifests summary
  • supported override fields

docs.title: Overrides
docs.text: Overrides let operators adjust profile parameters without modifying profile code.

docs.title: Field overrides
docs.text:
Use:

--override <slug>:<field>=<value>

Example:

dump-config \
  --profiles coder_app \
  --groups group-a \
  --override coder_app:cpu_limit=4 \
  --override coder_app:mem_limit=8G

docs.title: Supported fields
docs.text:
The CLI supports overriding:

  • cpu_limit
  • cpu_guarantee
  • mem_limit
  • mem_guarantee
  • image
  • groups

Example:

dump-config \
  --profiles coder_app \
  --groups group-a \
  --override coder_app:image=ghcr.io/eoepca/pde-code-server:latest-dev

docs.title: Type handling
docs.text:
• cpu_limit and cpu_guarantee must be integers
  • groups must be comma-separated list

Invalid CPU values fail fast:

dump-config \
  --profiles coder_app \
  --groups group-a \
  --override coder_app:cpu_limit=not_an_int

docs.title: Node selector overrides
docs.text:
Node selectors are overridden with:

--node-selector <slug>:<key>=<value>

Example:

dump-config \
  --profiles gpu_coder_app \
  --groups group-a \
  --node-selector gpu_coder_app:nodepool=gpu

Note: this merges with profile defaults (it does not replace them).

docs.title: CLI overview
docs.text:
The CLI entrypoint is:

dump-config

It generates an Application Hub YAML configuration.

docs.title: Help
docs.text: dump-config --help

docs.title: Main options
docs.text:
Usage: dump-config [OPTIONS]

  Generate an application-hub configuration YAML.

Options:
  --profiles TEXT           Comma-separated list of enabled profile slugs
                            [default: coder_app]
  --groups TEXT             Comma-separated list of groups  [default:
                            developers]
  --output TEXT             Output YAML file  [default: config.yaml]
  --storage-class-rwo TEXT  StorageClass for ReadWriteOnce volumes
  --storage-class-rwx TEXT  StorageClass for ReadWriteMany volumes
  --node-selector TEXT      Override node selector for a profile. Format:
                            <slug>:<key>=<value>. Can be repeated.
  --override TEXT           Override profile attributes. Format:
                            <slug>:<field>=<value>. Can be repeated.
  --list-profiles           List available registered profile slugs and exit
  --describe-profile SLUG   Print a human-readable summary of a profile and
                            exit
  --profiles-dir DIRECTORY  Extra folder(s) containing python modules/packages
                            defining additional profiles. Modules must
                            register into profile_registry.
  --help                    Show this message and exit.

docs.title: Profile loading order
docs.text:
• Built-in profiles are registered
  • External profile folders are loaded (if any)
  • CLI resolves enabled slugs and builds config

docs.title: External profiles (plugins)
docs.text:
Configurator supports loading profiles from external folders using --profiles-dir.

This enables:

  • custom deployments
  • site-specific profiles
  • local experiments
  • profiles maintained outside the main repository

docs.title: Folder structure
docs.text:
Example plugin folder:

my-profiles/
├── my_coder_profiles.py
└── __init__.py

The folder can contain one or more Python modules. Those modules must import and register profiles into profile_registry.

docs.title: Example plugin module
docs.text:
from configurator.apps import profile_registry
from configurator.apps.coder.base_coder import BaseCoderProfile

class MyCustomCoder(BaseCoderProfile):
    slug = "my_custom_coder"
    display_name = "My Custom Coder"
    description = "Custom coder profile"

profile_registry.register(MyCustomCoder)

docs.title: Load plugins
docs.text:
dump-config \
  --profiles-dir ./my-profiles \
  --profiles my_custom_coder \
  --groups group-a \
  --output config.yaml

docs.title: Unknown profile slug
docs.text:
If you see:

Error: Unknown profile slug '...'

Run:

dump-config --list-profiles

docs.title: Invalid override format
docs.text:
Override format must be:

<slug>:<field>=<value>

Example:

--override coder_app:cpu_limit=4

docs.title: YAML contains escaped strings
docs.text:
This happens if multi-line values are treated as plain strings.

Configurator uses ruamel.yaml and wraps multi-line values as |.

If you add new models containing multi-line values, ensure they go through:

literalize_multiline_values()

docs.title: External profiles not loaded
docs.text:
Ensure plugin modules are top-level in the folder:

dump-config --profiles-dir ./plugins --list-profiles

If you don’t see your slug:

  • check sys.path importability
  • ensure the module registers into profile_registry

docs.title: Run the CLI with Docker
docs.text:
The configurator CLI can be executed directly from the Docker image.

This is useful when: - you don’t want to install Python locally - you want reproducible config generation - you want to mount external profiles/plugins into the container

docs.title: Build the image
docs.text:
From the project root:

docker build -t application-hub-configurator .

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
From the project root:

docker run --rm -it \
  -v $PWD/output:/work \
  -v $PWD/data:/data \
  application-hub-configurator \
  dump-config \
  --profiles-dir /data \
  --profiles coder_app \
  --output /work/config.yaml \
  --groups group-2

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
--profiles-dir allows loading extra profile modules/packages dynamically (plugin-style).

This is the recommended approach for:

  • site-specific profiles
  • experimental profiles
  • profiles not shipped with the core configurator repository

Examples in this repository:

  • training_how_to_app
  • mlflow_coder_app

If you are deploying via Kubernetes/Helm in this repository, also see the Skaffold-based flow in skaffold.yaml and the operator onboarding guide.

docs.title: Volume mounts
docs.text:
You typically want:

  • one mount for the output config location
  • one mount for external profiles (plugins)

Example layout:

  • /data/... contains external profiles
  • /work/... contains your output folder

docs.title: Recommended pattern
docs.text:
docker run --rm -it \
  -v $PWD/output:/work \
  -v $PWD/extra-profiles:/extra-profiles \
  application-hub-configurator \
  dump-config \
  --profiles-dir /extra-profiles \
  --profiles my_custom_coder \
  --groups group-2 \
  --output /work/config.yaml

This produces ./output/config.yaml on your host

docs.title: Adding Profiles
docs.text: Profiles are regular Python classes that inherit from a base profile family and register themselves into profile_registry.

docs.title: 1. Pick the right family
docs.text:
Use an existing family when the runtime behavior already matches your app:

  • BaseCoderProfile
  • BaseRemoteDesktopProfile
  • BaseJupyterLabProfile

Only create a new family if you need a new set of shared defaults or hooks.

docs.title: 2. Add the profile class
docs.text:
Example:

from configurator.apps import profile_registry
from configurator.apps.coder.base_coder import BaseCoderProfile


class MyProfile(BaseCoderProfile):
    slug = "my_profile"
    display_name = "My Profile"
    description = "Example profile"
    image = "ghcr.io/example/my-profile:latest"


profile_registry.register(MyProfile)

Required class attributes:

  • slug
  • display_name
  • description
  • image

Common optional attributes:

  • cpu_guarantee, cpu_limit
  • mem_guarantee, mem_limit
  • default_url
  • bash_login_path
  • bashrc_path
  • init_script_path

docs.title: 3. Place the profile in the correct package
docs.text:
Built-in profiles live under configurator/apps/<family>/.

Typical pattern:

  • add the class to coder_profiles.py, remote_desktop_profiles.py, or jupyterlab_profiles.py
  • export it from the package __init__.py
  • register it in that same __init__.py

Example registration in configurator/apps/coder/__init__.py:

from configurator.apps import profile_registry
from .coder_profiles import CoderProfile, GpuCoderProfile

profile_registry.register(CoderProfile)
profile_registry.register(GpuCoderProfile)

docs.title: 4. Add supporting files if needed
docs.text:
The codebase uses file-backed assets for shell setup and manifests.

Common locations:

  • configurator/apps/<family>/config_maps/...
  • configurator/apps/<family>/manifests/...

Profiles reference these assets through explicit paths in Python, for example:

import os

base_path = os.path.dirname(__file__)
bashrc_path = os.path.join(base_path, "config_maps/my_profile/bash-rc")
init_script_path = os.path.join(base_path, "config_maps/my_profile/init.sh")

There is no automatic convention-based loading. If you add a file, you must wire it in from Python.

docs.title: 5. Override hooks only when needed
docs.text:
Most profiles should override a small subset of hooks:

  • get_default_volumes() for additional storage
  • get_manifests() for structured Kubernetes resources
  • get_config_maps() for extra mounted files
  • get_pod_env_vars() for environment variables
  • get_extra_resource_limits() for GPU or other extended resources

Do not override build() unless you are changing the output contract itself.

docs.title: 6. Add tests
docs.text:
At minimum, add or extend tests for:

  • successful CLI generation with the new slug
  • any profile-specific overrides
  • manifests if the profile emits them
  • plugin loading if the profile is meant to be external

Useful test files to mirror:

  • tests/test_cli_dump_config.py
  • tests/test_cli_overrides.py
  • tests/test_cli_manifests_dumping.py
  • tests/test_external_profiles.py

docs.title: External profiles
docs.text:
For site-specific or experimental profiles, prefer external plugin modules loaded with --profiles-dir.

Behavior today:

  • every top-level Python module/package inside the provided folder is imported
  • imported modules are expected to register into profile_registry
  • duplicate slugs fail fast

Minimal external profile example:

from configurator.apps import profile_registry
from configurator.apps.base import BaseAppProfile


class ExternalProfile(BaseAppProfile):
    slug = "external_profile"
    display_name = "External Profile"
    description = "Loaded from --profiles-dir"
    image = "alpine:3.19"


profile_registry.register(ExternalProfile)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Configurator builds an Application Hub YAML file from Python profile classes.

The runtime is organized around five layers:

  • registry: stores concrete profile classes by slug
  • profile families: provide shared defaults and hooks for a class of apps
  • CLI: resolves user input, loads profiles, applies overrides, and writes output
  • models: Pydantic schema for the generated configuration
  • IO/helpers: YAML serialization plus config map / manifest helpers

docs.title: Main modules
docs.text:
• configurator.main Thin module that exposes the CLI entrypoint by importing configurator.cli.commands.main.
  • configurator.cli.commands Defines the dump-config Click command and all supported options.
  • configurator.plugins.loader Imports built-in profile packages and optionally imports external plugin modules from --profiles-dir.
  • configurator.apps.registry.ProfileRegistry Central in-memory registry keyed by profile slug.
  • configurator.apps.base.BaseAppProfile Base class that assembles a Profile Pydantic object.
  • configurator.models Pydantic models for profiles, volumes, role bindings, manifests, config maps, and the final Config.
  • configurator.io.yaml_writer Writes the final YAML using ruamel.yaml.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
1. dump-config starts in configurator.cli.commands.main.
  2. Built-in profiles are registered by importing:
  3. configurator.apps.coder
  4. configurator.apps.remote_desktop
  5. configurator.apps.jupyterlab
  6. External profile folders passed through --profiles-dir are added to sys.path, then every top-level module/package in those folders is imported.
  7. CLI arguments are parsed into:
  8. enabled profile slugs
  9. groups
  10. node selector overrides
  11. attribute overrides
  12. Each selected profile class is looked up in profile_registry, instantiated, and optionally overridden.
  13. BaseAppProfile.build() converts the profile instance into a configurator.models.Profile.
  14. All built profiles are wrapped in configurator.models.Config.
  15. configurator.io.yaml_writer.write_yaml() serializes the config to disk.

docs.title: Registration model
docs.text:
Profiles do not use auto-discovery inside the repository.

Registration happens explicitly at import time in package __init__.py files, for example:

from configurator.apps import profile_registry
from .coder_profiles import CoderProfile

profile_registry.register(CoderProfile)

This keeps profile availability deterministic and makes test setup straightforward.

docs.title: Profile lifecycle
docs.text:
BaseAppProfile exposes hooks that subclasses override to contribute data:

  • get_default_volumes()
  • get_manifests()
  • get_role_bindings()
  • get_config_maps()
  • get_image_pull_secrets()
  • get_env_config_maps()
  • get_env_secrets()
  • get_secret_mounts()
  • get_pod_env_vars()
  • get_extra_resource_limits()

Concrete profiles should define identity and defaults through class attributes such as:

  • slug
  • display_name
  • description
  • image
  • cpu_guarantee, cpu_limit
  • mem_guarantee, mem_limit
  • default_url
  • optional file-backed paths like bashrc_path and init_script_path

build() is implemented once in BaseAppProfile and should normally not be overridden.

docs.title: Built-in profile families
docs.text:
• configurator.apps.coder Registers coder_app, gpu_coder_app, and coder_dask_gateway_app.
  • configurator.apps.remote_desktop Registers remote_desktop, qgis_remote_desktop, panoply_remote_desktop, and snap_remote_desktop.
  • configurator.apps.jupyterlab Registers jupyterlab_small.

Each family packages its own defaults, supporting config maps, and manifests alongside the Python classes.

Deployment-specific profiles such as training or product add-ons should live in external plugin folders loaded with --profiles-dir.

docs.title: Overrides
docs.text:
Overrides are handled in two steps:

  • configurator.overrides.parser Parses --override and --node-selector CLI values.
  • configurator.overrides.apply Validates and applies attribute overrides to instantiated profiles.

Examples:

  • coder_app:cpu_limit=4
  • gpu_coder_app:image=ghcr.io/example/gpu:latest
  • gpu_coder_app:nodepool=gpu

docs.title: YAML output
docs.text:
The final config is emitted through ruamel.yaml.

Important behavior:

  • manifests are written as structured YAML objects, not YAML-encoded strings
  • multi-line config map content is preserved as literal blocks where applicable
  • output is based on the Pydantic model graph, not ad hoc dict assembly

docs.title: Manifests
docs.text:
Profiles can attach Kubernetes manifests to the generated YAML through the manifests field.

In this project, manifests are stored as structured YAML documents, not as raw strings.

docs.title: Why structured manifests matter
docs.text:
Raw YAML strings are hard to read and hard to post-process:

content: "---\napiVersion: ..."

Structured output is the intended representation:

content:
  - apiVersion: v1
    kind: ServiceAccount

This is also what the test suite validates.

docs.title: Loading manifests
docs.text:
Use configurator.apps.app_helpers.load_manifests():

from configurator.apps.app_helpers import load_manifests


def get_manifests(self):
    return [
        load_manifests(
            name="local-stack-coder-app",
            key="local-stack",
            file_path="/path/to/manifest.yaml",
            slug=self.slug,
        )
    ]

Current helper signature:

def load_manifests(*, name: str, key: str, file_path: str, slug: str) -> Manifest:
    ...

Behavior:

  • reads one file containing one or more YAML documents
  • parses documents with yaml.safe_load_all
  • drops empty documents produced by ---
  • returns a Manifest Pydantic object with persist=False

docs.title: Template placeholders
docs.text:
Manifest files may contain template placeholders that are intended for later rendering by the consumer side, for example:

  • {{ namespace }}
  • {{ spawner.user.name }}

Configurator preserves these values when loading and writing the YAML.

docs.title: Recommended layout
docs.text:
Keep manifest files close to the profile family that owns them, for example:

  • configurator/apps/coder/manifests/...
  • configurator/apps/remote_desktop/manifests/...

The loader is path-based, so the exact folder name is a project convention, not a hard requirement.

docs.title: Testing manifests
docs.text:
If a profile emits manifests, add tests that verify:

  • manifests are present in the generated config
  • content is structured YAML data, not a string
  • each document includes expected Kubernetes keys such as apiVersion and kind

Relevant tests:

  • tests/test_cli_manifests_dumping.py

docs.title: Release
docs.text: This repository is packaged with Hatch and publishes a wheel built from the local source tree.

docs.title: Version source
docs.text:
The project version is defined in:

  • configurator/__about__.py

pyproject.toml reads that file through:

[tool.hatch.version]
path = "configurator/__about__.py"

docs.title: Recommended release workflow
docs.text:
1. Update configurator/__about__.py.
  2. Run tests.
  3. Run formatting and checks.
  4. Build the distribution artifacts.
  5. Validate the generated wheel in a clean environment or container.
  6. Tag the release in Git.
  7. Publish using your internal delivery process.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Run tests:

hatch run test:test-q

Run checks:

hatch run dev:lint
hatch run dev:check

Build docs:

hatch run docs:build

Build the wheel:

hatch build -t wheel

Build the container image that installs the wheel:

docker build -t application-hub-configurator .

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• the Dockerfile builds a wheel in a builder stage and installs that wheel in the runtime stage
  • there is no release automation documented in this repository beyond the local Hatch and Docker workflows
  • if you add CI-based publishing later, update this document to describe the exact registry and tagging rules

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Configurator uses pytest and click.testing.CliRunner.

Most tests execute the CLI and validate the generated YAML rather than testing internals in isolation.

docs.title: Running tests
docs.text:
If you use Hatch:

hatch run test:test-q

Available scripts from pyproject.toml:

  • hatch run test:test
  • hatch run test:test-q
  • hatch run test:test-cov
  • hatch run test:test-show-setup

If you use the task runner:

task test

That task currently runs hatch run test:test-show-setup.

docs.title: Test structure
docs.text:
Current coverage is organized around:

  • CLI generation: tests/test_cli_dump_config.py
  • overrides and node selectors: tests/test_cli_overrides.py
  • CLI failures and validation errors: tests/test_cli_failures.py
  • listing and describing profiles: tests/test_cli_list_describe.py
  • structured manifest dumping: tests/test_cli_manifests_dumping.py
  • external plugin loading: tests/test_cli_external_profiles.py and tests/test_external_profiles.py
  • registry behavior: tests/test_registry.py

docs.title: Test patterns
docs.text:
Common pattern:

  1. use CliRunner
  2. invoke configurator.main.main
  3. write output to a temporary file
  4. parse YAML with test helpers
  5. assert on generated structure

Example:

from click.testing import CliRunner

from configurator.main import main


def test_list_profiles():
    runner = CliRunner()
    result = runner.invoke(main, ["--list-profiles"])

    assert result.exit_code == 0
    assert "coder_app" in result.output

docs.title: Registry isolation
docs.text:
The suite uses autouse fixtures in tests/conftest.py to clear the global profile_registry between tests.

That matters because:

  • built-in profiles register at import time
  • plugin tests import external modules dynamically
  • duplicate registrations would otherwise leak across tests

docs.title: When adding tests
docs.text:
For a new profile or feature, prefer adding tests that exercise user-visible behavior:

  • successful config generation
  • override handling
  • failure messages for invalid input
  • manifest structure when YAML documents are involved

This keeps the suite aligned with the CLI contract.

docs.title: Developer onboarding
docs.text: This guide is for engineers adding or changing profile behavior.

docs.title: 1. Local setup
docs.text:
From repository root:

pip install hatch
hatch env create

Sanity check:

hatch run dump-config --help

docs.title: 2. Know the project layout
docs.text:
Start with:

  • configurator/apps/ for profile families and concrete profiles
  • configurator/cli/ for command-line behavior
  • configurator/plugins/ for external profile loading
  • tests/ for CLI and registry behavior coverage

docs.title: 3. Daily developer commands
docs.text:
task check
task test
task lint

docs.title: 4. Typical change flow
docs.text:
1. Add or modify profile code.
  2. Update tests in tests/.
  3. Update docs under docs/ when behavior changes.
  4. Run checks and tests locally.
  5. Open a pull request.

docs.title: 5. Recommended first reads
docs.text:
• docs/dev/architecture.md
  • docs/dev/adding-profiles.md
  • docs/dev/testing.md

docs.title: Maintainer onboarding
docs.text: This guide is for repository maintainers responsible for quality and releases.

docs.title: 1. Core responsibilities
docs.text:
• Review pull requests for correctness and backward compatibility
  • Ensure test and lint pipelines stay green
  • Maintain docs and release notes quality
  • Cut and publish tagged releases

docs.title: 2. Review checklist
docs.text:
1. Behavior change is covered by tests.
  2. Docs are updated for user-facing changes.
  3. No accidental breaking changes in profile slugs, CLI options, or schema.
  4. CI workflows still pass (package, docs).

docs.title: 3. Release checklist
docs.text:
1. Bump version in configurator/__about__.py.
  2. Confirm task test and task check pass.
  3. Tag the release (vX.Y.Z) matching project version.
  4. Push tag to trigger GitHub publish workflow.
  5. Verify package is published and installable.
  6. Validate Skaffold deployment profiles (baseline, develop, main) still point to expected hub image/tag and config file wiring.

docs.title: 4. Security and governance
docs.text:
• Follow SECURITY.md for vulnerability reporting.
  • Follow CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md for community interactions.
  • Keep templates in .github/ current for issues and PRs.

docs.title: 5. Recommended first reads

docs.title: Operator onboarding
docs.text: This guide is for platform operators generating Application Hub configuration.

docs.title: 1. Install and verify
docs.text:
Use one of:

pip install app-hub-configurator
dump-config --help

or from source:

hatch run dump-config --help

docs.title: 2. Generate your first config
docs.text:
dump-config \
  --profiles coder_app,gpu_coder_app \
  --groups group-a,group-b \
  --output config.yaml

docs.title: 3. Inspect what is available
docs.text:
dump-config --list-profiles
dump-config --describe-profile coder_app

docs.title: 4. Apply runtime overrides
docs.text:
dump-config \
  --profiles coder_app \
  --groups group-a \
  --override coder_app:cpu_limit=4 \
  --override coder_app:mem_limit=8G \
  --output config.yaml

docs.title: 5. Use external profile plugins
docs.text:
dump-config \
  --profiles-dir ./my-profiles \
  --profiles my_custom_profile \
  --groups group-a \
  --output config.yaml

docs.title: 7. Skaffold workflow (cluster deployment path)
docs.text:
If you deploy Application Hub through Helm/Skaffold, use the repository skaffold.yaml.

Typical flow:

  1. Generate config.yaml with dump-config.
  2. Deploy using one of the Skaffold profiles:
  3. baseline
  4. develop
  5. main

Example:

skaffold run -p develop

Notes:

  • skaffold.yaml injects config.yaml into the chart values (setFiles.configYml).
  • Image/tag selection is profile-based in Skaffold.

docs.title: Onboarding
docs.text:
This section helps new contributors and users ramp up based on their role.

Use the guide that matches your main responsibilities:

  • Developer onboarding
  • Maintainer onboarding
  • Operator onboarding

docs.title: Quick map
docs.text:
• If you write or modify profiles, start with developer onboarding.
  • If you review, release, and steward quality, start with maintainer onboarding.
  • If you run the tool to generate deployment configs, start with operator onboarding.

docs.title: Coder profiles
docs.text:
Coder profiles are based on BaseCoderProfile.

They provide:

  • workspace volume (/workspace)
  • calrissian volume (/calrissian)
  • bash config maps
  • init script
  • default CPU/memory values
  • optional manifests (e.g. Dask Gateway)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• coder_app
  • gpu_coder_app
  • coder_dask_gateway_app

Downstream examples loaded via --profiles-dir:

  • training_how_to_app
  • mlflow_coder_app

docs.title: Dask Gateway profile
docs.text:
coder_dask_gateway_app includes structured manifests:

  • Helm Release (Crossplane)
  • ConfigMaps
  • RBAC roles and bindings

docs.title: Profiles overview
docs.text:
Profiles are Python classes registered in the ProfileRegistry.

Each profile provides:

  • slug (unique key)
  • display_name
  • description
  • container image
  • default CPU/memory
  • volumes
  • config maps
  • init containers
  • manifests
  • role bindings
  • node selector
  • pod environment variables

docs.title: Built-in profile families
docs.text:
• Coder (code-server)
  • Remote desktop (noVNC-based)
  • JupyterLab

See:

  • Coder profiles
  • Remote desktop profiles

docs.title: Remote Desktop profiles
docs.text:
Remote desktop profiles provide a Linux desktop environment via browser (noVNC).

They are based on BaseRemoteDesktopProfile.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• remote_desktop
  • qgis_remote_desktop
  • panoply_remote_desktop
  • snap_remote_desktop

docs.title: Default URL
docs.text:
Desktop profiles set:

default_url = "/desktop"

docs.title: Config schema
docs.text:
The generated YAML follows the Application Hub schema:

profiles:
  - id: profile_coder_app
    groups: [...]
    definition:
      slug: coder_app
      display_name: ...
      description: ...
      kubespawner_override:
        cpu_limit: ...
        mem_limit: ...
    volumes: [...]
    config_maps: [...]
    manifests: [...]
    role_bindings: [...]

The canonical schema is defined by configurator.models.

docs.title: Why are profiles Python classes?
docs.text:
Profiles contain logic (volumes, config maps, manifests, defaults). Python provides:

  • reuse via inheritance
  • composition helpers
  • clear versioning in Git

docs.title: Can I override everything?
docs.text:
Only fields supported by CLI override parsing.

If you need more fields, extend:

  • apply_overrides()
  • documentation and tests

docs.title: How do I add my own profiles?
docs.text:
Use:

dump-config --profiles-dir ./my-profiles --list-profiles

docs.title: Tutorial: EOEPCA extra config with all profiles in extra-profiles
docs.text:
This tutorial shows how to generate a config.yaml that enables these applications in Application Hub:

Application Repository Processor Development Environment EOEPCA/pde-code-server JupyterLab EOEPCA/iat-jupyterlab Remote Desktop EOEPCA/iga-remote-desktop Remote Desktop with QGIS EOEPCA/iga-remote-desktop-qgis Remote Desktop with SNAP EOEPCA/iga-remote-desktop-snap Remote Desktop with Panoply EOEPCA/iga-remote-desktop-panoply Dashboard with Streamlit EOEPCA/iga-streamlit-demo

docs.title: 1. Create one external profile pack
docs.text:
Create a folder that contains all EOEPCA app profiles as plugin profiles:

mkdir -p data/work/eoepca-extra-profiles
cat > data/work/eoepca-extra-profiles/eoepca_profiles.py <<'PY'
from configurator.apps import profile_registry
from configurator.apps.base import BaseAppProfile
from configurator.apps.coder.base_coder import BaseCoderProfile
from configurator.apps.jupyterlab.base_jupyterlab import BaseJupyterLabProfile
from configurator.apps.remote_desktop.base_remote_desktop import BaseRemoteDesktopProfile


class EoepcaPdeProfile(BaseCoderProfile):
    slug = "eoepca_pde_app"
    display_name = "Processor Development Environment"
    description = "PDE Code Server"
    image = "ghcr.io/eoepca/pde-code-server:latest-dev"
    cpu_guarantee = 1
    cpu_limit = 2
    mem_guarantee = "4G"
    mem_limit = "6G"
    storage_class_rwo = "standard"
    storage_class_rwx = "standard"


class EoepcaJupyterLabProfile(BaseJupyterLabProfile):
    slug = "eoepca_jupyterlab_app"
    display_name = "JupyterLab"
    description = "EOEPCA JupyterLab environment"
    image = "ghcr.io/eoepca/iat-jupyterlab:latest-dev"
    cpu_guarantee = 1
    cpu_limit = 2
    mem_guarantee = "4G"
    mem_limit = "6G"
    storage_class_rwo = "standard"


class EoepcaRemoteDesktopProfile(BaseRemoteDesktopProfile):
    slug = "eoepca_remote_desktop"
    display_name = "Remote Desktop"
    description = "EOEPCA Remote Desktop"
    image = "ghcr.io/eoepca/iga-remote-desktop:1.2.0"
    cpu_guarantee = 1
    cpu_limit = 2
    mem_guarantee = "4G"
    mem_limit = "6G"
    storage_class_rwo = "standard"


class EoepcaQgisRemoteDesktopProfile(BaseRemoteDesktopProfile):
    slug = "eoepca_qgis_remote_desktop"
    display_name = "Remote Desktop with QGIS"
    description = "EOEPCA Remote Desktop with QGIS"
    image = "ghcr.io/eoepca/iga-remote-desktop-qgis:latest"
    cpu_guarantee = 1
    cpu_limit = 2
    mem_guarantee = "4G"
    mem_limit = "6G"
    storage_class_rwo = "standard"


class EoepcaSnapRemoteDesktopProfile(BaseRemoteDesktopProfile):
    slug = "eoepca_snap_remote_desktop"
    display_name = "Remote Desktop with SNAP"
    description = "EOEPCA Remote Desktop with SNAP"
    image = "ghcr.io/eoepca/iga-remote-desktop-snap:latest-dev"
    cpu_guarantee = 1
    cpu_limit = 2
    mem_guarantee = "4G"
    mem_limit = "6G"
    storage_class_rwo = "standard"


class EoepcaPanoplyRemoteDesktopProfile(BaseRemoteDesktopProfile):
    slug = "eoepca_panoply_remote_desktop"
    display_name = "Remote Desktop with Panoply"
    description = "EOEPCA Remote Desktop with Panoply"
    image = "ghcr.io/eoepca/iga-remote-desktop-panoply:latest-dev"
    cpu_guarantee = 1
    cpu_limit = 2
    mem_guarantee = "4G"
    mem_limit = "6G"
    storage_class_rwo = "standard"


class EoepcaStreamlitDashboardProfile(BaseAppProfile):
    slug = "eoepca_streamlit_dashboard"
    display_name = "Dashboard with Streamlit"
    description = "Interactive Streamlit dashboard"
    image = "ghcr.io/eoepca/iga-streamlit-demo:latest"
    default_url = "/proxy/8501/"

    cpu_guarantee = 1
    cpu_limit = 2
    mem_guarantee = "2G"
    mem_limit = "4G"


profile_registry.register(EoepcaPdeProfile)
profile_registry.register(EoepcaJupyterLabProfile)
profile_registry.register(EoepcaRemoteDesktopProfile)
profile_registry.register(EoepcaQgisRemoteDesktopProfile)
profile_registry.register(EoepcaSnapRemoteDesktopProfile)
profile_registry.register(EoepcaPanoplyRemoteDesktopProfile)
profile_registry.register(EoepcaStreamlitDashboardProfile)
PY

docs.title: 2. Generate config.yaml (with storage classes)
docs.text:
Run:

dump-config \
  --profiles-dir data/work/eoepca-extra-profiles \
  --profiles eoepca_pde_app,eoepca_jupyterlab_app,eoepca_remote_desktop,eoepca_qgis_remote_desktop,eoepca_snap_remote_desktop,eoepca_panoply_remote_desktop,eoepca_streamlit_dashboard \
  --storage-class-rwo managed-nfs-storage \
  --storage-class-rwx cephfs \
  --groups group-a,group-b \
  --output config.yaml

docs.title: 3. Optional: tune resources per profile
docs.text:
Use --override for per-profile CPU and memory:

dump-config \
  --profiles-dir data/work/eoepca-extra-profiles \
  --profiles eoepca_pde_app,eoepca_jupyterlab_app,eoepca_remote_desktop,eoepca_qgis_remote_desktop,eoepca_snap_remote_desktop,eoepca_panoply_remote_desktop,eoepca_streamlit_dashboard \
  --storage-class-rwo managed-nfs-storage \
  --storage-class-rwx cephfs \
  --groups group-a,group-b \
  --override eoepca_pde_app:cpu_limit=4 \
  --override eoepca_pde_app:mem_limit=8G \
  --override eoepca_jupyterlab_app:cpu_limit=4 \
  --override eoepca_jupyterlab_app:mem_limit=8G \
  --override eoepca_streamlit_dashboard:cpu_limit=2 \
  --override eoepca_streamlit_dashboard:mem_limit=4G \
  --output config.yaml

docs.title: 4. Validate the generated profiles
docs.text:
yq '.profiles[].definition.slug' config.yaml

Expected slugs include:

  • eoepca_pde_app
  • eoepca_jupyterlab_app
  • eoepca_remote_desktop
  • eoepca_qgis_remote_desktop
  • eoepca_snap_remote_desktop
  • eoepca_panoply_remote_desktop
  • eoepca_streamlit_dashboard

docs.title: 5. Validate resources and storage classes
docs.text:
Inspect resource limits:

yq '.profiles[].definition.kubespawner_override | {image, cpu_limit, mem_limit}' config.yaml

Inspect volume storage classes:

yq '.profiles[].volumes[].storage_class' config.yaml | sort -u

docs.title: 6. Deploy with Skaffold
docs.text:
If you deploy via the repository Helm/Skaffold flow:

skaffold run -p develop

skaffold.yaml injects config.yaml into the chart (setFiles.configYml in profile patches).

docs.title: 7. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Unknown slug errors: Ensure --profiles-dir data/work/eoepca-extra-profiles is passed.
  • Streamlit app route: If your image uses a different port/path, adjust default_url accordingly.
  • Profile discovery: Use dump-config --profiles-dir <dir> --list-profiles to confirm registration.
  • Duplicate slug errors: Keep custom slugs unique and avoid reusing built-in slugs such as coder_app or jupyterlab_small.
  • Resource override validation errors: Ensure CPU values are integers and memory values are valid strings (example: 8G).
